{{recipesummary|category=Sauce recipes|yield=2 cups|time=20 minutes|difficulty=2}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Sauces|Sauces]]

'''''Sauce velouté''''', takes its name from the adjectival form of the French word ''velour'', meaning velvet. In some older English cookbooks it is called ''velvet sauce''. It is one of the five "Mother Sauces" of [[Cookbook:Cuisine of France|French cuisine]].

== Ingredients ==
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* ¼ cup (60 g) [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 2 cups (480 ml) boiling [[Cookbook:White stock|white stock]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste
* White [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]], to taste

== Procedure ==
# Make a white [[Cookbook:Roux|roux]]: melt the butter in a sauce pan over low heat until the foam subsides. [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] in the flour and cook slowly, while stirring until the mixture froths up for about 2 minutes. The flour should lose its raw smell but not its color.
# Remove from the heat. When the ''roux'' has stopped bubbling, slowly incorporate the stock, whisking quickly but smoothly to create a smooth mixture.
# Add the seasonings and cook over medium-low heat, stirring frequently. Simmer the sauce until it lightly coats the back of a spoon.
# Taste and adjust seasonings.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
*If sauce is lumpy, force the sauce through a fine [[Cookbook:Sieve|sieve]] or process it in a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]].
* If sauce is too thick, thin it out with stock.
*If sauce is too thin, bring the sauce to a boil. Then, off the heat, blend in a ½ tablespoon of ''[[wikipapers:Beurre_manié|beurre manié]]'' with a wire whisk. Boil for 1 minute, stirring.
